title: Classify a Quarantined Morning
scenario: The feed arrived 27 minutes late and the SPP row is in quarantine. The brief still ships at 7:00. Classify what survived - and stamp every row with the degraded status, because a consumer who cannot tell a partial run from a full one will trust it like a full one.
inputLabel: Quarantine Notice + Surviving Data + Ratified Policy
input:
From the feed incident (see price-feed incident record): feed arrived 6:42; the SPP row was malformed and is QUARANTINED - held for the vendor, not dropped, expected back tomorrow. This run is DEGRADED.

Surviving rows (actual vs prior day):
ERCOT: actual 198, prior day 172
MISO: actual 81, prior day 77

Threshold Policy v2.0.0, as ratified by the desk from the historical redesign: routine at 6 percent or more, escalate at 16 percent or more (day-over-day, size of move). Desk rounding: 1 decimal.

Propagation rule: on a degraded run, every emitted row carries degraded: true so downstream consumers inherit the warning with the data.
instructions: Compute each surviving hub's pctMove: (actual - priorDay) / priorDay * 100, rounded to 1 decimal.
Classify against the RATIFIED v2.0.0 bands: 6 and 16.
SPP is quarantined, not dropped: emit no SPP row, and do not invent one.
Stamp every row with degraded: true per the propagation rule.
Return a JSON array, then validate.
copilotPrompt: Classify a degraded run: compute pctMove = (actual - priorDay) / priorDay * 100 rounded to 1 decimal for ERCOT (198/172) and MISO (81/77), classify with bands 6 (routine) and 16 (escalate), omit the quarantined SPP row, and stamp every row degraded: true. Return a JSON array of { hub, pctMove, status, degraded }.
successMessage: Degraded run classified. Every row carries its warning label - partial data that admits it is partial stays trustworthy.

intro.heading: Before you build: partial runs must say so

sections.title: Degraded is a status, not an apology
sections.body: The run is incomplete by DESIGN - the runbook chose quarantine over guessing. Propagating degraded: true on every row turns that choice into data, so the brief and any later consumer can label what they show.

sections.title: Quarantined is not dropped
sections.body: Medium tier dropped a poisoned row for good. Quarantine is different: the SPP row is held as evidence and expected back once the vendor fixes it. Today's job is to leave a hole shaped exactly like SPP - visible, temporary, uninvented.

sections.title: The redesigned policy changes the story
sections.body: ERCOT moved 15.1 percent - under the OLD 12-percent rule that escalates; under the ratified v2.0.0 (escalate at 16) it is routine. A big-looking number that does not escalate is the redesign working as intended: the desk chose rarer escalations, on evidence.

sections.title: No escalation, no approval
sections.body: With both survivors below 16, this brief will release without a sign-off - on a morning with an active incident. That is correct under the rules, and it is exactly why the degraded stamp matters: the label does the warning work the approval will not.

fieldGuide.hint: Two hubs survived. The third is quarantined, not yours to invent.
Bands are 6 and 16 now - check the intro's ERCOT story.
The propagation rule applies to every row.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd combine the clean prices and the policy into one judgement per hub - normal, watch, or breach - so a human sees a single verdict.

bestFit.how: a 'Switch' on the computed score to assign a risk label
a scoring node that writes the label into state, with the rubric passed in as config
a scoring function returning both the score and the reason it fired

takeaway.heading: Quarantined morning classified
points: You computed and classified only what survived, leaving a visible SPP-shaped hole instead of an invented row.
Every row carries degraded: true - the run's condition travels WITH the data, not in a log nobody joins against.
You watched the redesigned policy change an outcome: 15.1 percent is routine under ratified v2.0.0, where the old rule would have escalated.
The degraded brief you assemble next inherits both the classifications and the warning label.
The workflow can now classify honestly on a partial run and make sure every consumer knows it was partial.
